articles.title: Super League Club Gradings: Wakefield Trinity catapult to top of 'optional' 2026 rankings after stunning Grand Final triumph
articles.summary: From 2026, completion of Super League's Club Grading process was not mandatory, with final ranking reflecting clubs who chose to take part rather than a ranking of every club across Super League and the Championship; Wakefield, ranked eighth in 2025, shoot to top after stunning campaign
articles.body:
From 2026, completion of the Grading process was not mandatory. The final ranking therefore reflects the clubs who chose to take part in grading, rather than a ranking of every club across Super League and the Championship.

The West Yorkshire club, who won the Super League Grand Final on Saturday to end a 58-year wait for title glory , scored 17.85 out of a maximum 20 across the grading model.

It was the highest score achieved by any club in 2026 (and joint-highest ever with Hull KR in 2025), coming after they finished eighth in last year's process which is run by the RFL.

Trinity, one of eight clubs to secure a Grade A (15 points plus), also recorded the biggest year-on-year increase of any club at +2.38 points, boosted by 0.75 bonus points for their Grand Final triumph under the Performance pillar.

Grading involves five pillars - Fandom, Finance, Stadium, Community and On-Field Performance.

Wakefield were relegated from Super League in 2023 after receiving an indicative grading score of 12.52 (11th), then won the Championship Grand Final in 2024 to return to Super League with Grade A status, reached the Super League Play-Offs in 2025, and have now combined a Grand Final-winning season with first place in the rankings.

All 14 clubs who featured in the top 14 last year have retained their places and they are now automatically guaranteed a spot in Super League in 2027.

Wakefield become the fourth different club in as many years to take top spot since the process began, following on from Leeds Rhinos (2023), St Helens (2024) and Hull KR (2025).

Leeds (17.03) are second, beaten Grand Finalists Warrington Wolves (16.72) third and League Leaders Shield winners Wigan Warriors (16.46) fourth. Last year's Treble winners Hull KR are fifth (16.45), with Leigh Leopards (16.31), St Helens (15.59) and Castleford Tigers (15.03) completing the eight clubs to achieve Grade A status in 2026.

Castleford regain Grade A in eighth place with a score of 15.03, having been 11th in 2025. Catalans Dragons (14.83) and Hull FC (14.72) have dropped from Grade A to Grade B after slipping from seventh and ninth respectively to ninth and 10th.

Bradford Bulls (13.93), Huddersfield Giants (13.50), Toulouse Olympique (13.44) and York Knights (13.24) complete the 14 and are all classed as Grade B.

A dozen Championship clubs took part in the process - some for their own benchmarking purposes only - with five Grade B clubs emerging.

Barrow Raiders are the highest-ranked Championship club in 15th and Grand Final winners London Broncos moved up to 16th.

Doncaster RLFC made the second-highest year-on-year gain, improving by +1.36 points and climbing from 23rd to 17th after facing London in Sunday's title decider, while Widnes Vikings also claimed Grade B status.

Ian Nolan, RFL chief executive, said: "Wakefield Trinity's rise to the top of the 2026 Club Grading rankings is a fascinating story for Rugby League, and a strong example of how sustained progress on and off the field can be recognised through the grading framework.

"Their achievement sits alongside encouraging movement across the sport, from growing attendances and digital audiences to continued improvements in facilities and community delivery. The RFL will keep working with clubs to support responsible growth, long-term resilience, and the strongest possible future for the professional game."

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Michael McArdle's side begin long road to Brazil with World Cup play-off
articles.summary: Northern Ireland defenders Nat Johnson and Rebecca Holloway tell BBC Sport NI of their dream of reaching a first ever Women's World Cup as NI go through the play-offs.
articles.body:
A World Cup staged in Brazil is the stuff of dreams for any footballer and the chance to experience that is on offer for Northern Ireland as they begin their play-off journey against Portugal with hope of securing a spot at next year's tournament.

It will be a difficult ask for Michael McArdle's side, which has been hit by a spate of injuries and features five new faces, but there is a quiet confidence in the group before what will be, for some of them, the biggest games in their careers to date.

First up, in what is set to be an arduous journey in search of a World Cup debut, is Friday's home leg at Inver Park (19:30 BST) against the Portuguese.

"When you're growing up, Brazil is the place to be, it's the home of football. It really doesn't get much better than that," said Norwich City defender Natalie Johnson.

"The fact that we are at this point and that it could be a reality, you don't need much more motivation than that.

"There's a lot on the line, but we are taking it one game at a time and I think if you look at it that way, nothing is impossible. Obviously there is that dream at the end of it, but we're focused on the game in front of us."

Family, football and Dalglish - what drives NI boss McArdle?

What will new call-ups bring to Northern Ireland?

Elmore and Grant named in Northern Ireland squad

'We are going in to get something out of this'

As one of the lowest-ranked European sides in the play-offs, it is a difficult route to next summer's tournament for Northern Ireland.

If they overcome Portugal they will then face Croatia or Iceland in the next round. If they make it through those games, they will likely have an inter-continental play-off to make it the whole way to Brazil.

Portugal inflicted two defeats on in NI in Euro 2025 qualifying and sit 28 places higher in the Fifa world rankings, but Johnson and her side are not daunted by the task in front of them and instead want to embrace it.

"We absolutely believe these games are winnable," she added.

"We have a lot of experience in this team and the young players coming in bring their own individual experience and they really add to the squad. It's a good balance and we are going in to get something out of this.

"Any Portugal side is going to be very technical and we're expecting a very fast-paced game. We're going to have to be at our best to face that, quick football, and that's what we're working towards.

"On paper it might look like there is a big gap between the teams, but at the end of the day, it is a game of football and I think particularly on our home pitch it will be a much more level playing field."

NI's men's team an inspiration for McArdle's youngsters

Birmingham City defender Rebecca Holloway is one of the few survivors from the squad that qualified for Euro 2022, NI's first major tournament.

There have been a lot of changes to the squad since, but Holloway is excited for the future rather than dwelling on past achievements.

"It feels like a long time ago in a way, especially when you look at how much the squad has changed, but I think that's also what is very exciting," she said.

"It's like a new generation coming through and I think it's also important that we have some experienced players here to help those new faces. We're excited to see what they can do and encourage them to play with confidence and freedom and do what they are good at.

"We're slowly closing the gap on Portugal and the so-called bigger nations. They had a narrow 2-1 win over us at home in 2024 after a 4-0 away defeat, I think that shows that we are getting closer."

McArdle's youthful side do not have far to look for inspiration as to how to punch above their weight.

After assembling in camp on Monday, the team watched Northern Ireland's men's side 0-0 draw with Georgia.

That stalemate ensured Michael O'Neill's side stayed top of their Nations League group after picking up eight points from four games without conceding a goal.

"It was brilliant watching them play with such youth and energy and the exciting football that they are playing.

"This younger generation play with no fear and I think that is what the men's senior team are doing.

"I am hoping the young players see that and we can adopt the same attitude. I think we were all watching thinking we can't wait to do this on Friday."

articles.title: Why WWE Money in the Bank Has a Very Different Feel This Year
articles.summary: While WWE once had a Big Four of premium live events, that number has increased to five since Money in the Bank became a yearly event.
articles.body:
WWE has a "Big Four" premium live events in each year, but that number has arguably increased to five since Money in the Bank became an annual addition to the calendar.

This show has as much impact on the immediate future of WWE as the Royal Rumble and sometimes creates the even bigger surprises.

In recent years, though, Money in the Bank has felt like a concept running out of steam, becoming almost a burden on the brand rather than a boon.

However, the 2026 edition of MITB in New Orleans on Saturday feels different. But why? Well, it all starts with perception...

The last three Money in the Bank PLEs have been run under the creative focus of Triple H, who has focused on strong stars each year to win big.

The winners of the men's and women's Money in the Bank ladder matches are Damian Priest and Iyo Sky (2023), Drew McIntyre and Tiffany Stratton (2024), and Seth Rollins and Naomi (2025).

Other top names who have picked up big wins at these events include Cody Rhodes, Gunther, Sami Zayn and Becky Lynch.

The booking has been strong, and the winners regularly went on to play big roles in the company for years to come.

However, the feeling coming out of these shows was muted. Most of the cash-ins were completed within a month, and the other results felt secondary to building hype toward Survivor Series.

Most importantly, even with fresh names such as Sky and Stratton winning, it never felt like WWE had a plan to make the most of their status as Money in the Bank victors.

This year, WWE has presented a stacked line-up focused on the top stars of now and the future.

Roman Reigns is working a singles match at the show for the first time since 2021.

Stephanie Vaquer, Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan are competing in the most consequential women's non-ladder match since at least 2022.

Bronson Reed and Oba Femi are fighting for the right to be seen as the new top monster in WWE right now.

Most importantly, both MITB ladder matches are stacked, not with top names but top prospects.

The women's match especially is a fresh NXT-trained line-up including all first-time potential winners except Tiffany Stratton, who is still only 27 years old and on the rise.

The possibility of fresh stars emerging is high, and the air of this show feels different.

Money in the Bank should be the match that focuses most on the up-and-coming stars of WWE.

Bron Breakker, Trick Williams and Je'Von Evans highlight a fresh line-up of younger names. Even Penta (41) and Kevin Owens (42) may not be young anymore but are exciting new names near the top of the card.

Jacy Jayne, Roxanne Perez, Sol Ruca, Lola Vice and Lash Legend are all names that WWE has not seriously pushed yet with a decade of potential ahead of them that could be unlocked with a win.

The fact that Oba Femi is already established well enough to get a singles match on this card instead of throwing him into the ladder match speaks to WWE's new focus.

CM Punk and Roman Reigns are the main representatives of the old guard in WWE on the card, and that is only because they are the top two stars in the company right now.

WWE has a chance to make lasting statements on its direction with this show in a way Money in the Bank has not done in recent years.

The goal for Money in the Bank 2026 should be to make clear that multiple new stars are on the rise and taking the power from WWE's reliable veterans.

This is not the time to hold back. Bron Breakker, Roxanne Perez, Oba Femi, Stephanie Vaquer and others should be walking out with big wins.

Moreover, those not winning need clear direction that will carry them through the rest of the year.

With a strong foundation and massive potential, the right booking could show this night to be a true turning point in WWE history.

Carry that momentum forward, and fans will be eagerly awaiting WrestleMania 43 for its potential to solidify a new fresh focus for all of WWE.

articles.title: 10 Most Expensive Sports Jersey Sales of All Time
articles.summary: In September, a game-worn Michael Jordan jersey from Game 3 of the 1998 NBA finals sold for $12,260,000, claiming the No. 2 spot on the list of the most expensive sports jersey sales in history.
articles.body:
In September, a game-worn Michael Jordan jersey from Game 3 of the 1998 NBA finals sold for $12,260,000, claiming the No. 2 spot on the list of the most expensive sports jersey sales in history.

Sports memorabilia has become an investment tool, similar to fine art in recent years. It has seemingly become a monthly occurrence that a new piece of sports history hits the auction block and sells for millions.

Zooming in specifically on the jersey market, we've highlighted the 10 most expensive jersey sales of all time. As the latest Jordan sale shows, this is an extremely fluid leaderboard that could be reshaped again in the near future.

NBA Players with the All-Time Most Career Earnings💰

10 MOST EXPENSIVE SPORTS JERSEYS OF ALL TIME

Sale Price: $24,120,000 | Date: August 2024

At this point, whether or not Babe Ruth actually called his shot before homering in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series is irrelevant. It's become one of the most iconic tales in baseball history. This is the jersey he wore in that game.

The jersey was originally acquired in 1990 from an elderly woman in Florida whose father was a golfing buddy of Ruth's after his retirement. It sold for $940,000 in 2005, before it was specifically verified to be from Game 3. That provenance has helped make it the most valuable piece of sports memorabilia ever sold.

Sale Price: $12,260,000 | Date: September 2026

Sold by JOOPITER, the auction house founded by Pharrell Williams, this jersey surpassed the record mark set by the Game 1 jersey from the same series for the most expensive non-sports-card piece of Michael Jordan memorabilia. While Game 1 was a Bulls loss, Game 3 was the most lopsided victory in NBA Finals history, with Chicago winning 96-54 behind a game-high 24 points from Jordan.

Sale Price: $10,091,000 | Date: September 2022

This jersey blew past expectations, as Sotheby's had a projected $3-5 million sale price. It ultimately more than doubled the high end of that figure, making it the most valuable jersey of all time prior to the Ruth sale. The Bulls actually lost Game 1 in overtime against the Utah Jazz, with Jordan scoring a game-high 33 points.

Diego Maradona's handball goal in the 1986 World Cup quarterfinals against England stands as one of the defining moments in soccer history, largely because of the quote he later gave.

"A little with the head of Maradona, and a little with the hand of God."

The "Hand of God" ball from that same play also recently sold, fetching $3,355,000 in August 2026.

Sale Price: $7,004,000 | Date: April 2025

Photo matching technology has linked this jersey to NBA Media Day, Bryant's preseason debut (Oct. 16, 1996), his regular-season debut (Nov. 3, 1996) and five other games from his rookie season. It previously sold for a more modest $115,242 at auction in 2012, representing an increase of nearly 6000% in a little over a decade.

Sale Price: $5,850,000 | Date: February 2023

One of the lasting images of Kobe Bryant's career was him letting out a yell after knocking down a clutch three-pointer in Game 2 of the 2008 Western Conference First Round against the Nuggets. This is the jersey he wore when he hit that shot. It has been linked to 25 total games, giving it a unique level of game action relative to most modern jerseys.

Sale Price: $5,640,000 | Date: June 2019

Hunt Auctions sold this Ruth jersey in a live auction at Yankee Stadium in 2019. It was the most expensive piece of sports memorabilia ever sold at the time. The previous record belonged to a 1920 Ruth jersey, which sold for $4,415,658 in 2012.

Sale Price: $5,246,000 | Date: August 2025

This jersey is not only signed and game-worn, but also photomatched by MeiGray and SIA to multiple games during the 1960 season, including the 1960 All-Star Game, where Mantle was the starting center fielder for the American League. The Yankees star led the AL with 40 home runs during the 1960 campaign, hitting .275/.399/.558 for a 162 OPS+ and finishing runner-up to teammate Roger Maris in AL MVP balloting.

Sale Price: $4,900,000 | Date: September 2023

This jersey was worn in Game 5 of the 1972 NBA Finals, when the Lakers clinched the franchise's first championship since moving to Los Angeles. A 35-year-old Chamberlain averaged 19.4 points and 23.2 rebounds in the series, including an impressive 24-point, 29-rebound performance while playing with a broken hand in Game 5.

Sale Price: $4,880,000 | Date: July 2026

Pelé announced himself to the world at the 1958 World Cup, still shy of his 18th birthday. He scored six goals in four matches, including two in the final against Sweden. He still stands as the youngest player ever to appear in and score in a World Cup Final. This was the shirt he was wearing when he carved out that place in history.

While it didn't fit on this leaderboard since it was not a single jersey sale, it's worth mentioning that the set of six Lionel Messi jerseys from the 2022 World Cup sold for $7,800,000 in December 2023, which is another hugely significant sale on the sports jersey timeline.

Likewise, a 1951 game-worn jersey and 1950 game-worn pants combination from Brooklyn Dodgers legend Jackie Robinson sold for $5,520,000 in August 2024. It was excluded from our leaderboard since the two-piece uniform did not cleanly fit the criteria.

It's only a matter of time before the next piece of sports history hits the auction block and the final sale price makes national headlines, but for now, the list stands as the largest confirmed sales in history for a sports jersey.

articles.title: Ranking the 15 Greatest WWE Money in the Bank Cash-Ins
articles.summary: The Money in the Bank cash-in has become one of WWE's greatest moments each year, highlighting fresh talent and delivering dramatic changes to the title scene.
articles.body:
The Money in the Bank cash-in has become one of WWE's greatest moments each year, highlighting fresh talent and delivering dramatic changes to the title scene.

Not all cash-ins are created equal, though.

While stars have risen throughout the years after capturing the briefcase, some have made lasting marks with their cash-ins that changed WWE.

The following are the 15 greatest MITB cash-ins ever from Seth Rollins and CM Punk to Naomi and Tiffany Stratton.

While Money in the Bank cash-ins are mostly a major success for WWE, there have been some notable duds over the years that made the concept feel like a waste of time.

John Cena - Raw 1000: It is never necessary to give a star as big as Cena the MITB briefcase, but it did mean WWE's first failed cash-in did not hurt the talent. It just felt pointless. Cena defeated CM Punk by disqualification after Big Show interfered. He failed to win the championship, not the match.

Damien Sandow - Raw, October 28, 2013: If Cena's cash-in was supposed to avoid hurting young talent, Sandow's cash-in was the opposite. This was as rough a burial as they come, losing clean after cashing on a vulnerable GOAT.

Baron Corbin - SmackDown, August 15, 2017: For a stretch of time in WWE, the company booked like MITB was more a burden than a booking hook, and it culminated with Corbin getting rolled up by Jinder Mahal and never getting anywhere near a world title again.

Braun Strowman - Hell in a Cell 2018: Strowman called his shot against Roman Reigns inside Hell in a Cell, and somehow the match ended by no contest via Brock Lesnar interference. This was a complete waste of everyone's time.

Theory - Raw, November 7, 2022: It was bad enough that he was a last-minute addition to the 2022 ladder match and won, but Theory remains the only wrestler to cash in on a midcard title, the United States Championship. And he failed! This is the worst cash-in of all time.

Cash-in moments have defined many fans' WWE experience, and there will be some seen in higher regard by some that will not be included in this list of 15.

Sheamus - Survivor Series 2015: This was a core moment for the rise of Roman Reigns as WWE's Big Dog but felt like a poor recreation of Randy Orton's cash-in on Daniel Bryan with diminished results.

Liv Morgan - Money in the Bank 2022: While fans lived in the moment as Morgan finally won the big one, the underdog babyface came out of this looking like she was not ready, and fans turned against her in the following months.

Damian Priest - WrestleMania XL Night 2: It was nice to see Priest reach the top of the business, but it was more important for Drew McIntyre vs. CM Punk than Priest himself. WWE showed little faith in him as champion until he lost to Gunther.

Seth Rollins - SummerSlam 2025 Night 1: WWE tried to deliver a new "heist of the century" with Rollins' second cash-in, but the convoluted "work the audience" angle of his injury did not serve much story purpose on top of a real injury derailing his run not long after.

15. CM Punk - Monday Night Raw, June 30, 2008

CM Punk was one of the first stars to truly elevate themselves through the Money in the Bank concept.

The two-time winner made the most of his first chance in 2008 when he cashed in on the man whose legacy is most tied to the briefcase, Edge, to win his first World Heavyweight Championship.

While it was a fairly simple setup and payoff as Punk took advantage of Batista laying out The Rated-R Superstar, this effectively delivered an audience-approved message: Punk is ready.

An unfortunate injury ended his reign after just 68 days, but it set a foundation that The Best in the World would build upon.

In particular, it set up one of the best cash-ins of all time just one year later.

14. Edge - Friday Night SmackDown, May 11, 2007

Edge earned his moniker of The Ultimate Opportunist with his first cash-in, but his second truly solidified the name.

The same week he took the briefcase from Mr. Kennedy, he cashed in on The Undertaker to take the World Heavyweight Championship.

While the moment was pre-taped and spoiled online ahead of time, it almost made the moment bigger as fans were left in shock by the wild title change before it even aired.

The Rated-R Superstar will forever be known first for his original run with the briefcase, but this cash-in was just as important to Edge's own career as it set him on a path to win even more world titles for years to come.

13. Carmella - SmackDown, April 10, 2018

The first woman to win the Money in the Bank briefcase, Carmella has still held the contract longer than anyone in WWE's history.

She made the most of carrying around the briefcase, proving how valuable it can be to be Miss Money in the Bank before ever winning the title at the end.

When she did cash in, she took advantage of a vulnerable Charlotte Flair just after WrestleMania and won her only world title.

Her title reign did not quite live up to the buildup, but it did solidify the value of Carmella, who was an integral star through the rest of her WWE career.

12. The Miz - Monday Night Raw, November 22, 2010

Looking back, The Miz was not ready to win the WWE Championship in 2010, but it felt like he would be.

After a strong run as United States champion, The A-Lister got his biggest break by winning Money in the Bank.

He stalked Randy Orton until the time was right to strike, cashing in on a weakened Viper who had just retained against Wade Barrett.

The match was competitive as Orton tried to fight through injury to keep his title, but ultimately Miz stole the gold and got the biggest opportunity of his career to run with it.

Even if The A-Lister was not ready, WWE took a massive risk that solidified him as a mainstay on screen for years to come.

He would even come around to cash in the title in less impressive fashion in 2021. He is the first-ever double Grand Slam champion and one of only two of all time alongside Seth Rollins.

That legacy began with this cash-in and served as a blueprint for future new-star opportunities utilizing Money in the Bank.

11. Big E - Monday Night Raw, September 13, 2021

It is bittersweet looking back at what Big E could have been in WWE, but back in 2021, he was on the rise.

Coming off a successful run as intercontinental champion, Big E captured Money in the Bank and quickly declared his intention to cash in on the September 13 Raw.

Bobby Lashley was already set to face Randy Orton that night, so it was not a clean cash-in. However, Big E still overwhelmed The All Mighty to take the gold and defeated him clean in a rematch.

The moment felt special because Big E was a special talent, but WWE wavered by the end of the year.

In 2022, Brock Lesnar took the belt from Big E, and the former champion would go back to working as a tag wrestler with The New Day.

Nothing went right after the cash-in, but at least before his likely career-ending injury, Big E got his moment to stand atop WWE with complete crowd support.

Following Carmella's cash-in, WWE went years without a female winner holding the Money in the Bank briefcase for more than a day.

That changed with Iyo Sky, even if she still only held it for 35 days.

The Genius of the Sky was one of the biggest beneficiaries of the creative shift to Triple H, who had booked her big throughout her time in NXT.

One year after her debut at SummerSlam 2022, Sky became the WWE women's champion and a much-deserved victor. She had delivered time and again, but fans were growing tired of waiting for her to get her time at the top.

She cashed in on the woman she had been feuding with most often throughout the year, Bianca Belair, who had just regained the WWE Women's Championship from Asuka.

Sky would go onto dominate the women's division, establishing herself as one of the best wrestlers in the entire company.

Her reign ended at WrestleMania XL Night 2 by delivering one of the best women's matches in 'Mania history against Bayley.

A year later, she became women's world champion at WrestleMania 41, further establishing herself as the ace of the women's division.

9. Tiffany Stratton - SmackDown, January 3, 2025

A babyface turn by cash-in is a rare sight in WWE, and this was the biggest moment of Tiffany Stratton's career.

While The Center of the Universe was popular from the moment she arrived in WWE, she especially gained popularity under the thumb of Nia Jax.

Stratton helped Jax take the WWE Women's Championship from Bayley at SummerSlam 2024, only to quickly begin targeting her ally, even bringing in Candice LeRae to help with the bullying.

Fans rallied around Stratton, who won Money in the Bank before finally snapping at Jax. She cashed in the briefcase in January 2025 to take the gold.

While most cash-ins are surprises, this felt like an inevitable moment realized, which allows it to stand out among the rest as a fresh use of the briefcase.

Stratton is now established as one of WWE's most reliable stars and could well add more titles to her legacy this year.

Of the 34 Money in the Bank cash-ins in WWE history, only eight have been women, which was a number the men reached in 2010.

That makes it difficult for the women's division to match up to the legacy of the men's division in terms of memorable cash-ins.

Still, Naomi stands out for the best cash-in by any woman so far in WWE history.

It took seven years for the women's division to receive a second Evolution PLE, and it was clear that everyone involved was ready to make the most of the spotlight.

In the main event, Rhea Ripley and Iyo Sky delivered one of the best matches on 2025, only to be undercut by the first-ever women's mid-match cash-in courtesy of Naomi.

For months since her MITB win, The Glow had teased cashing in on WWE women's champion Tiffany Stratton, only to switch it up at the last minute.

It was a genuine shock and delivered an unforgettable finish to Evolution, signaling that a heel Naomi was about to take over.

However, that did not happen yet as Naomi stepped away to become a new mother with real-life husband Jimmy Uso.

When Naomi returns, the legacy of this moment should be defined better by how high she can go in WWE.

Randy Orton has rarely needed another world title reign. As a 14-time world champion, few can match his legacy.

However, The Viper's cash-in on Daniel Bryan at SummerSlam 2013 was less about Orton's legacy and more about the man he defeated.

Bryan had fought through painfully bad booking to fight John Cena in the most important match of his WWE career.

The Yes! Man delivered an unforgettable match and a rare clean win over The GOAT, seemingly becoming the new top star of WWE.

However, as suddenly as Bryan reached the top, he crashed back down courtesy of a Triple H betrayal and Orton cash-in.

While The Authority angle that followed was far more miss than hit, there has never been a cash-in that started such a massive shift in the business.

This was the moment when all the heels aligned to take over the company and make Bryan the company's top underdog.

Even if fans still had to push to get him there, this is the moment that set up WrestleMania XXX as one of WWE's greatest nights.

6. Dean Ambrose - Money in the Bank 2016

When discussing the legacy of The Shield, WWE has often discounted the third man, Dean Ambrose, due to him leaving the company in 2019.

However, this story is a three-man show, and that was felt more than any other moment in 2016.

Roman Reigns walked in as WWE champion, facing his long-time rival Seth Rollins. Before that main event, though, The Lunatic Fringe captured the Money in the Bank briefcase.

When Rollins successfully overwhelmed Reigns to capture the championship, Ambrose's music hit.

He ran down to take out his former friend and rival Rollins, avenging two years prior when Rollins had stolen the Money in the Bank from him with the help of The Authority.

Ambrose cashed in and successfully defeated Rollins to take the WWE Championship, finally winning the gold both of his Shield brothers had already held.

On this night, all three members of The Shield were WWE champion, and that solidified how important the group was to WWE.

5. Dolph Ziggler - Monday Night Raw, April 8, 2013

On paper, nothing sounds too remarkable about Dolph Ziggler cashing in on an injured Alberto Del Rio on the Raw after WrestleMania.

In the moment, though, it was pure magic.

A long-running veteran was finally getting his due, and a raucous internal audience still around after 'Mania wanted Ziggler to get his win.

It did not matter that Del Rio was supposed to be the babyface or that Ziggler was technically the heel.

Fans cheered overwhelmingly for the victory for The Showoff, who never truly got his fair shake in WWE.

An unfortunate concussion sidelined Ziggler not long after this win, and he quickly dropped the title back to Del Rio.

WWE though did pull a double turn in that match, fueled by the fan reaction from that Raw after WrestleMania, and fans would continue to cheer on Ziggler for years to come despite management losing faith.

4. Rob Van Dam - ECW One Night Stand 2006

Before WWE grew obsessed with only using Money in the Bank for the cash-in payoff, Rob Van Dam set a unique standard for the briefcase that has not been replicated.

RVD did not want to cheat his way to finally winning the top prize in WWE. He wanted to win it on his home turf.

He challenged John Cena to meet him at ECW One Night Stand in the Hammerstein Ballroom in front of a raucous fan base of ECW loyalists.

This set up the most singularly hostile crowd Cena has ever performed in front of, delivering a spectacle that stands strong in the legacy of both men.

While the Edge interference was unnecessary and RVD did not get to be champion for long, it is hard to not get nostalgic thinking about the atmosphere of this match.

It is a shame that more MITB winners do not use the briefcase like this more often, setting up unforgettable home field advantages to redefine their legacies.

The rules of the Money in the Bank briefcase were well established by the time CM Punk won it for the second year in a row at WrestleMania.

However, fans had not seen anything like what The Best in the World was about to do with the case.

For the first time in WWE, a babyface was going to use the case to not only win gold but turn heel on the same night.

It was the perfect setup and payoff, elevated by Punk's opportunistic move the previous year.

He would make clear he was always going to cash in on the winner of the brutal ladder match between Edge and Jeff Hardy, no matter who walked out the victor.

However, he became a hated figure for doing so at the expense of The Charismatic Enigma, who had never gotten a real chance to run as WWE's top champion.

It sparked a rivalry that would end Jeff's run with WWE at that time on a major high and give Punk the platform necessary to show he was ready to be the next big star.

After years of WWE seemingly running out of ways to use the Money in the Bank briefcase, Seth Rollins delivered a shocker on The Grandest Stage of Them All.

The Architect did not wait until after Brock Lesnar vs. Roman Reigns was complete. Instead, he cashed in during the match to make it a Triple Threat.

He then took advantage of a beaten-down Big Dog to win Lesnar's WWE Championship and stand tall with his first world title.

This was the culmination of WWE's post-Shield plans. Less than one year after the breakup of the group, Rollins was the world champion and Reigns was on the hunt for revenge.

It delivered a compelling hook for the coming months as many tried to figure out what they could do to stop the crafty Rollins and The Authority.

This could be argued to be the best cash-in due to its shocking twist, including Rollins rebounding after losing to Randy Orton earlier in the same night.

However, it is hard to beat the true originator of the concept.

It is easy to talk about the legacy of Money in the Bank now as a guarantee, but there was a time where nothing was certain.

WWE did not even truly know what the briefcase could be used for when Edge won it at WrestleMania 21.

However, The Rated-R Superstar held the contract for 280 days and planned out an idea that had never been done before in WWE.

He cashed in his title shot on a vulnerable John Cena, left nearly broken after retaining his WWE Championship inside the Elimination Chamber and beat him after two Spears.

It was a genuinely shocking scene that solidified Edge as a new top heel and would begin a long-term rivalry between The Rated-R Superstar and The GOAT.

Even though Edge's title reign did not last long, he would go on to become an 11-time world champion in WWE and a Hall of Fame headliner off this moment.

articles.title: World Rally Championship: Rally Scotland to take place in autumn as 2027 calendar released
articles.summary: The inaugural Rally Scotland will take place from 30 September-3 October as the 2027 World Rally Championship calendar was released.
articles.body:
The inaugural Rally Scotland will take place from 30 September-3 October in an extended 2027 World Rally Championship (WRC) calendar released by the FIA and the sport's promoters.

The gravel event in Aberdeenshire will form the 12th round of a 15-event calendar, as it joins the USA as new events on the schedule.

It is the first time the United Kingdom has hosted a round of the WRC since 2019, and BBC Sport will provide extensive live coverage of the rally.

It will also be a home round for new World Rally champion Elfyn Evans, who won the title in dramatic circumstances in Sardinia on Sunday after rival Oliver Solberg crashed at the end of the final stage.

In doing so, Evans became the first WRC champion from the UK in 25 years and joined the late Colin McRae and Richard Burns as the sport's top-level title winners.

Northern Ireland drivers Josh McErlean and Jon Armstrong also competed at the top level of the sport in 2026 and will be aiming to return next year.

In addition to Rally Scotland, the BBC's coverage will include five live stages plus the Power Stage on all WRC rounds, highlights programmes, plus digital clips and content across BBC platforms.

How Evans defied history to join rallying greats

Evans ends Britain's 25-year wait for WRC champion

The season will start on the icy tarmac roads in Monte Carlo from 21-24 January before rounds in the snow in Sweden and vast landscapes of Safari Rally Kenya.

Three tarmac events in a row then take place in Croatia, the Canary Islands and Japan, before the Acropolis Rally in Greece.

The WRC's Italian round moves from September to July, and will switch from the gravel roads of Sardinia to tarmac in Rome.

The high-speed events in Estonia and Finland retain their back-to-back summer slots before the USA hosts its first WRC round in 39 years from 26-29 August.

The WRC last held a points-paying round in the USA at the Olympus Rally in 1988, and the championship will return as a gravel round after a successful candidate event in June.

Rally Scotland takes place in early October before a South American double-header, in Paraguay and Chile, and Rally Saudi Arabia round out the calendar.

A Saudi Arabia race was set to end the 2026 season but it was cancelled because of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Rally de Portugal will not feature in the 2027 calendar but is in talks to return in 2028.

The upcoming season will mark a new era for the sport with the introduction of a new promoter along with WRC27 regulations which will limit costs and reduce the horsepower of the top cars.

It will also mark the return of Ford as a manufacturer to the sport in a collaboration with the M-Sport banner.

articles.title: Así es la 'operación Messi' para entrar en el Cornellà
articles.standfirst: El futbolista argentino inicia su proyecto en el equipo catalán con esta operación, que valora el 100% del capital en torno a 1,4 millones de euros y por la que pasará a controlar hasta el 80%
articles.summary: El futbolista argentino inicia su proyecto en el equipo catalán con esta operación, que valora el 100% del capital en torno a 1,4 millones de euros y por la que pasará a controlar hasta el 80%
articles.body: Cuánto pagó Leo Messi y su grupo inversor para comprar la UE Cornellà es uno de los grandes interrogantes de esta operación corporativa. El futbolista argentino liderará una ampliación de capital de 1,1 millones de euros que se aprobó el pasado junio y que servirá para concretar la adquisición del club barcelonés de Tercera Federación, según documentación a la que ha tenido acceso 2Playbook. La operación supone valorar el 100% del club en torno a 1,37 millones de euros, ya que la entrada de dinero se realizará mediante la emisión y puesta en circulación de 4.400 nuevas acciones a un valor nominal de 250 euros cada una. En caso de que ninguno de los accionistas actuales acudan inicialmente a la compra de títulos, la participación de Messi se situará en torno al 80%. Las nuevas acciones tendrán el mismo valor que las existentes hasta la fecha, y los actuales accionistas del Cornellà tendrán un mes desde hoy para ejercitar su derecho de suscripción preferente y adquirir un número de títulos proporcional al valor de las que ya poseen en la entidad. La entrada de dinero permitirá reforzar el balance de la UE Cornellà, que a cierre de 2024-2025 disponía de un patrimonio neto positivo de 270.000 euros. La huella de Messi ya se evidencia en la estructura organizativa del club barcelonés, en el que ya entraron tras la reunión dos hombres de confianza de Messi, Alfonso Nebot y Pablo García Montañés. El primero de ellos es director del family office del astro argentino. Hace diez días también se sumó Aldo Guillermo Dallape como apoderado solidario. En el campo, la llegada de Messi a Cornellà también ha impulsado la entrada de nuevos patrocinadores para alimentar unos ingresos que rondan los 1,8 millones de euros si se incluyen las subvenciones. Pocas semanas después del anuncio de la compra del club, el neobanco MyInvestor se convirtió en patrocinador principal del club, con presencia del logo en el frontal de la camiseta verde. Esta financiera, respaldada por Andbank, El Corte Inglés Seguros y AXA España, tiene como uno de sus impulsores al ya mencionado García Montañés. El nuevo consejero del Cornellà es también director general adjunto del Grupo Andbank. El UE Cornellà es un club con gran reconocimiento en Cataluña, sobre todo, por su trabajo de cantera. En su fútbol base se han formado jugadores de la talla de Jordi Alba, David Raya, Gerard Martín, Javi Puado, Aitor Ruibal, Keita Baldé o Ilie Sánchez, entre otros. Además, este equipo de la periferia de Barcelona se ha convertido en el punto de partida de las inversiones de Messi en el fútbol español. El pasado viernes, el CD Eldense confirmó la llegada del ganador de ocho Balones de Oro al club de LaLiga Hypermotion con un modelo igual al del Cornellà: mayoría accionarial y, a priori, en solitario. Fuera de España, el futbolista del Inter Miami cuenta también con un club creado desde cero en su Rosario natal, Leones FC, y es socio de Luis Suárez en el Deportivo LSM de Uruguay. Además, ha promovido la Messi Cup, un torneo en el que compiten algunas de las mejores canteras del mundo.

articles.title: ‘Sneaky Advantage’: Ben Roethlisberger Explains Why Steelers Could Benefit From Colts’ London Trip
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a disappointing loss to the Cleveland Browns; however, Ben Roethlisberger sees one factor that could quietly work in t...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a disappointing loss to the Cleveland Browns ; however, Ben Roethlisberger sees one factor that could quietly work in their favor against the Indianapolis Colts .

Both teams enter Week 5 at 2-2; however, their paths into the matchup have been very different. The Colts just returned from a trip to London, while the Steelers played on Thursday night at home and had extra time to recover before Sunday's game. Roethlisberger believes that difference could matter more than people realize.

Ben Roethlisberger Spots Steelers' Rest Advantage Against Indianapolis Colts

Speaking on October 7, Roethlisberger pointed to the scheduling situation as a potential edge for the Steelers. The former Steelers quarterback admitted it may not be the biggest storyline heading into the game; however, he would keep it in mind.

"My one other little sneaky stat is, Indy is coming off a short week traveling to London. Pittsburgh's coming off a Thursday night game at home. There's a little bit of time, a little bit of rest. To me, that's like a little sneaky something. I do think that that short travel week, the Steelers having off, will be beneficial. Especially the Steelers got the weekend off, that'll be big for me".

The Colts played the Washington Commanders in London on Sunday, earning a 30-13 victory before beginning the trip back to the United States. The Colts had to deal with the travel involved in an overseas game while preparing for another road matchup just days later.

Pittsburgh, meanwhile, played Cleveland on Thursday night. That loss was a rough one for the Steelers; however, the early-week game gave them a longer runway to prepare for the Colts. That extra time could be especially useful for a team that has plenty to clean up after the Browns game. The Steelers struggled on both sides of the ball against the Browns and now have to turn their attention to a Colts team that has won two straight.

The Steelers also have the benefit of returning home for the matchup. Indianapolis will make another trip after its London excursion, while Pittsburgh has spent the week preparing at home . The former QB point is not that the scheduling advantage guarantees a Steelers win. Instead, it gives the Steelers one small edge in a game where the teams otherwise enter with identical records.

The Colts have shown they can be dangerous, taking the Kansas City Chiefs to overtime earlier this season before beating the Commanders in London. Indianapolis running back Jonathan Taylor also remains a major concern for Pittsburgh's defense.

Yet, the 44-year-old believes that the Steelers' additional recovery time should not be overlooked. After a frustrating loss in Cleveland, Pittsburgh needs to respond quickly. The extra rest gives the Steelers an opportunity to do exactly that, and according to their former quarterback, it could be one of the quieter factors working in their favor on Sunday.

articles.title: Brendan Bett says Florida needed humbling loss at Missouri
articles.summary: Brendan Bett called Florida's loss at Missouri a humbling experience and discussed the maturity needed to respond against South Carolina.
articles.body:
Brendan Bett believes Florida needed the humbling experience it received during a 45-17 loss at Missouri.

The veteran defensive lineman said complacency crept in following the Gators' 4-0 start, allowing weaknesses to remain hidden behind victories. He challenged the team to respond with greater maturity while refusing to blame the secondary for Florida's defensive struggles.

Bett also discussed the defensive line's search for a dominant performance, the challenge South Carolina's rushing attack presents and the intensity he expects from Florida's practices this week.

Where Florida's Aaron Philo ranks among first-year starting quarterbacks

How would you characterize the defensive line's performance against Missouri?

I feel like we came out with the right mindset and the right motor. Before the two big runs, they only had, I think, about 40 rushing yards.

We didn't get as many sacks as we would have liked, but I think we came out with good effort and made a good attempt to attack.

Was the Missouri loss a humbling experience?

Absolutely. It definitely was a humbling experience. I think people got a little complacent. In my opinion, I'm kind of glad it happened because we got to see where our true weaknesses were. Now, we can go and build off that.

Is it easier to grow from a loss than a win?

Absolutely. Like Coach says, when you win, our weaknesses get masked behind the victory. You really don't get to see everything because, "Hey, we got the win." But when you lose, all of that gets exposed. That's when you can go make corrections.

What is your role as a leader following the loss?

Mainly, it's keeping my guys hungry but humble at the same time and telling them that we can always play much better.

In my opinion, the defensive line hasn't had a dominant game yet. That's what we're striving for — to go out and have a dominant game. Regardless of whether we win or lose, I want us to have a dominant performance.

What challenges does South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers present?

We've played quarterbacks who can get loose, so I think the approach is always the same: Go get after him. But he can put it in the air, and he can move. They have a pretty good, strong running back.

This will probably be one of the most physical offenses we play. Coming off a loss, I think we have the right mindset about what we need to do.

How important is improving the team's maturity?

To be an absolutely good unit all around, you have to have maturity. It isn't just on game day. It's in the small details, starting today. How do we approach today? How do we do the things we need to do today, tomorrow and Wednesday that lead into Saturday?

What did you like about Sumrall's response to the loss?

The main thing Coach told us as soon as we entered the locker room was, "I love you guys. No matter what, I love you guys."

That's a great feeling. But, at the same time, he let us know that he's always going to hold us accountable. Obviously, that was nowhere near the standard we wanted. He made sure to let us know that.

He does a really good job of not just yelling and screaming. He coaches and makes corrections. He doesn't just tell you what you did wrong. He explains how you can do it better.

How is the defensive line supporting Florida's secondary?

I told them, "This is never just on y'all. We could have gotten more sacks. We could have put more pressure on the quarterback."

It's not just on them. What we need to do better is play together and understand that we're always going to be with each other.

We have those guys' backs. We let them know, "No matter what, we've got your back. Keep your heads up. We're going to get this right, and we'll be just fine."

Was Jeramiah McCloud's clapping penalty an example of the defense needing greater maturity?

I know he didn't mean any harm with that penalty. It just happened. We told him, "Remember, you can't clap. We'll get a delay of game for that."

Before the play, he was pumped up because it was third down. He told me, "Hey, let's go," and he clapped. We made the correction, and he knows now that he can't clap.

How did complacency develop during Florida's undefeated start?

We were coming off our fourth win. We had been rolling and doing pretty well. You can become complacent, not necessarily by feeling like you're just going to roll into a win, but by starting slowly.

I feel like that's what we did. We didn't start as fast as we normally do. When that catches up to you, it's hard to play from behind. That's where the complacency rolled in.

Will it be difficult to address that complacency this week?

I don't think it will be that hard. It's going to be addressed, of course. After the game, we had to soak it in and sit in it. But the thing I love about this team is the chemistry we have.

Everyone understood, "Hey, bro, that wasn't it." Everybody took ownership of their performances. Nobody was pointing fingers. We all understood what it was.

Even today, we came out with the mindset that it happened and we're going to put it behind us. Moving forward, we've got to go. We understand what we have to do now.

I feel like it was probably one of our best Monday practices. Was it maybe because of the loss? Probably. But it was also because everybody understood that we can't be complacent.

Everybody was rolling today. The defensive line was intense during individual drills. The secondary was going through seven-on-seven, and it was pretty intense.

That's a great way to stack our days. Coach always preaches going 1-0, but it doesn't just start Saturday. It starts today. Go 1-0 Monday. Go 1-0 tomorrow. Go 1-0 Wednesday. Then, when we get to Saturday, go 1-0 as well.

What do you expect from Tuesday's practice?

I'm hoping it's super intense. I'm hoping it's probably one of the hardest practices we have. You need those days. You need those hard practices to endure and to get your mind and body right.

How would you feel about playing in rainy, muddy conditions?

I love that because they've got to run the ball. I like that they're not going to throw the ball as much. I consider myself a run-stopper, so I prefer for them to run the ball and for me to make tackles, tackles for loss and stuff like that.

Hopefully, it gives us a little bit of an advantage as well.

What is the challenge against South Carolina's running game?

They're pretty physical, and they have a really good back. Since SEC play started, they've been averaging almost 200 yards per game.

We've got to go out there and assert that they're not going to be able to run the ball. The key is to stop the run. That's when you generate sacks.

Did Florida defend Missouri's rushing attack well before the two long runs?

Yes, sir. People who just look at the stats will see that he had 200 yards.

But when you know the full story, he didn't have those yards until the two big runs. Those runs should have never happened, and we're making corrections on that.

Beforehand, they had almost 50 yards going into the fourth quarter — 47. I feel like we did a pretty good job before those plays.

How have you improved at processing adversity?

The blessing is that I've been in worse situations.

I've gone through situations where I learned how to overcome adversity. With something like this, I'm able to maintain a good mindset for myself and help my teammates the best way I can without dwelling on it.

We've just got to keep moving forward. We have an opportunity to perform Saturday. That's where my mindset is, and I think that's the team's mindset as well.

articles.title: Brazilian women's league sees record crowd and audience growth in 2026
articles.summary: Women's A1 final sets attendance and TV audience recordsCredits: Rebeca Reis/Staff Images Woman/CBFThe 2026 season was historic for women's football in Brazi...
articles.body:
Women's A1 final sets attendance and TV audience records Credits: Rebeca Reis/Staff Images Woman/CBF

The 2026 season was historic for women's football in Brazil. In total, 52 million Brazilians watched Brasileirão Feminino A1 matches on TV Globo, the competition's broadcast rights holder, with record figures in the Northeast, Southeast and South regions. The final, which secured the title for São Paulo last Saturday (3), reached 23 million viewers.

The 52 million viewers recorded in 2026 make this season the most watched in three years. The record also reflects the popularity the sport has gained among key audience segments, with growth among women, socioeconomic classes A and B, teenagers aged 12 to 17 and young adults aged 18 to 24.

The national average audience rating was 10 points, 34% higher than the ratings of the three main competing free-to-air broadcasters. The increase in viewership was a nationwide phenomenon: Salvador recorded its highest-ever rating, at 12.1 points.

Rio de Janeiro recorded 11.4 points; São Paulo, 10.1; Recife, 10; Curitiba, 9.5; and Porto Alegre, 8.7. All these state capitals recorded their highest ratings in three years during this season.

The peak came in the competition's decisive final, when 23 million Brazilians watched the match on TV Globo. While the national average audience rating was 12.3 points, Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo recorded the two highest-ever ratings for women's football in Brazil, at 14.4 and 13.6 points, respectively.

Online, the topic also became a trend: content related to the Brasileirão Feminino reached 23 million views on the championship broadcast rights holder's social media accounts, eight times the figure for the 2025 edition. During the final, #BrasileirãoFeminino remained among Brazil's Trending Topics for two hours.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy’s Role With Giants Revealed After Latest QB Move
articles.summary: The New York Giants have made another change to their quarterback room. The team promoted Jake Haener from the practice squad to the active roster, moving hi...
articles.body:
The New York Giants have made another change to their quarterback room. The team promoted Jake Haener from the practice squad to the active roster, moving him behind starter Jameis Winston. The decision quickly raised questions about what it means for J.J. McCarthy .

The Giants now must decide how to divide roles among their quarterbacks and continue McCarthy's growth. Looking at Haener's promotion and the team's new depth chart may explain the plan behind this surprising move.

Giants promote Jake Haener to 53-man active roster

The Giants are adding Jake Haener to the 53-man roster after moving him up from the practice squad. Jameis Winston remains the starter, and the promotion gives New York a third quarterback available for game-day planning. The roster adjustment follows J.J. McCarthy's arrival from Minnesota after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. The move also gives New York flexibility for injuries, game-day substitutions, and practice planning. It now protects the team from having to carry only two available quarterbacks into a demanding weekly schedule.

"The Giants are signing QB Jake Haener to their 53-man roster off their practice squad, sources say. He joins J.J. McCarthy on the active roster behind Jameis Winston," NFL insider Mike Garafolo reported . The report confirms Haener's promotion, but it does not identify the move as a demotion for McCarthy.

McCarthy was the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft and is still learning New York's offense after the trade. Haener's addition gives the Giants more injury protection without changing Winston's starting status as New York prepares to face Washington in Week 5.

Jake Haener's promotion secures Giants depth without affecting J.J. McCarthy

New York's quarterback room has changed since Dart's knee injury. Winston stepped into the starting role, and McCarthy joined the roster after beginning the season in Minnesota. Haener had worked with McCarthy as the backup, giving the Giants an emergency option. Winston's recent improvement also explains why the team can develop McCarthy without rushing him.

Dan Duggan's explanation places the promotion in context : "This will enable them to activate all three QBs again, although more likely that McCarthy takes over as QB2 soon and Haener becomes the emergency third QB." McCarthy's role update points toward that path. McCarthy is positioned to slide into the primary backup slot once fully acclimated, leaving Haener to step into emergency duties.

That structure gives New York depth behind Winston without closing McCarthy's path. McCarthy remains firmly on track for the primary backup role, while Haener's addition secures necessary depth.

articles.title: Isack Hadjar calls for F1 cooling vests to be banned: "It's supposed to be tough"
articles.summary: Red Bull Formula 1 drivers Isack Hadjar and Max Verstappen have criticised cooling vests
articles.body:
Red Bull Formula 1 driver Isack Hadjar believes cooling vests should be banned from the championship, insisting that the extreme physical challenge remains an important part of motor racing.

The topic of cooling vests resurfaced at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia due to the extreme heat and humidity at the Sepang International Circuit. But the implementation of the equipment has been met with mixed feedback from drivers.

While some drivers welcome the artificial cooling, others have raised concerns regarding the fit and the effectiveness of the system. It seems to work well for a few laps by pumping cool liquid around the body through tubes in a fireproof top worn underneath the race suit, but as things heat up inside the cockpit, so does the liquid in the tubes.

When asked where he stood amid the differing views across the grid, Hadjar was clear in his position, arguing that artificial cooling aids have no place in F1.

"I think it should be banned. Because it's supposed to be tough," the Red Bull driver explained to Motorsport.com and other media in Singapore.

Hadjar's team-mate, four-time champion Max Verstappen , also claimed the cooling vest was "not needed", explaining that he would not use it even if it stayed cool for the duration of a whole grand prix.

"For me it's not needed," the Dutchman said. "Yes, it's hot, but it's not a sauna, and with this cooling vest you have these stupid cables in your car, so it's just limiting your movement as well.

"I don't need it, even if it would work for one and a half hours, like cool, cool, I don't need it, but it doesn't work anyway for one and a half hours. I don't think it has worked for one and a half hours in any category."

If a heat hazard is declared, teams and drivers have the option of wearing their own cooling vest systems or carrying ballast instead so there is no weight disadvantage for those wearing the vests.

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .
